topic: Most quotes are sent once and never followed up, not even a single time.

slides.subtitle: (not even once)
slides.scene: A single sheet of blank white paper curled slightly on a truck dashboard in cold morning light, dust visible on the vinyl, a pen wedged in the air vent. All vehicles, buildings, doors and surfaces in shot have COMPLETELY BLANK panels with absolutely no writing, no company name, no logo, no lettering, no phone number and no graphics of any kind. No signage anywhere in the scene. There is NO text, no words, no numbers and no labels anywhere in the image.

caption:
Did you know most quotes get sent once and never followed up at all?

Not chased twice. Not chased once. Sent, and then left alone until the contractor quietly writes it off.

There are good reasons. Following up feels like pestering, you are busy, and if they wanted it they would ring. Except they were not ignoring you. They got distracted, the quote moved down their inbox, and the one contractor who sent a short message four days later is the one who got the job.

The uncomfortable part is that this is free. It is not a lead cost, it is not advertising. It is one message to somebody who already asked you for a price.

And it never happens, because it has to happen on a specific day, and that day you were on a roof.
